newsitem.title: ITALY: Krupp could expand in Italy - board member.
newsitem.headline: Krupp could expand in Italy - board member.

text.p: German steel and engineering group Fried. Krupp AG Hoesch-Krupp has not ruled out increasing its presence in Italy, its most important foreign market ahead of the U.S. and Britain, a Krupp board member said.

Ulrich Middelmann said during a meeting with institutional investors in Milan that apart from the steel sector, "we are ready to reinforce our presence in other areas if there are good opportunities."
Among the group's core activities, Krupp' interest in Italy was above all focused in the components and engineering fields, he said without elaborating.
Middelmann said there had been contacts in France on the possible acquisition of the 28 percent stake in auto parts maker Valeo held by Cerus. "But it was too expensive just for 28 percent," he said.
He said Krupp did not like having minority stakes. "We discussed ways of going beyond 28 percent," but this had not been possible, he added.
After posting a group net profit in 1995 of 505 million marks, Krupp sees 1996 net profit slightly down after first half pre-tax profits fell 17 percent to 185 million marks.
In the special and stainless steels sector the 1995 pre-tax profit was 466 million marks. The 1966 result "will remain in three figures, but will however be significantly lower," Middelmann said.
This was due to a sharp fall in prices and excess capacity which will only be eliminated from the market in the next 18 to 24 months, he said.
